column3: The Hebrew says Moses “said” rather than “thought,” and calls the sight “great.”
The Hebrew explicitly says to remove the sandals “from your feet.”
The Hebrew uses the verb “serve” where BSB has “worship.”
The Hebrew verb can be expressed as “I will be”; the same first-person form recurs three times.
The Hebrew has one visitation expression governing both the people and what is done to them, rather than a separate “have seen.”
The object is “Egypt,” rather than explicitly “the Egyptians.”
The Hebrew names silver and gold “articles,” not specifically jewelry, and ends with “Egypt.”
